title: Recent errors gave no clear six-month PDO forecast gain for 1981-2025 targets
abstract: We tested whether recent forecast errors improved six-month Pacific Decadal Oscillation forecasts. A fixed linear model used current and previous PDO and annual harmonic terms. Each fit and correction used only observations available at its issue month. We scored 540 monthly targets in 1981-2025. Adding the mean of the last 60 available forecast errors raised mean squared error by 0.03%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -16.51% to +15.30%. Three- and ten-year correction windows also gave no clear gain. Thirty-year training and an added time predictor left the main result uncertain. This is a null result for a specified correction rule. It does not establish constant ocean response or constant forecast bias. Revised data, a scalar surface index, one lead and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, aggregate scores, a figure, an independent numerical audit and an exact archived-input retrieval path support reproduction.
